sanskrit: evamādyā manuṣyāṇāṃ strīṇāṃ ca bharatarṣabha śuśrāva madhurā vācaḥ punaḥ punar udīritāḥ
english: Such, O bull of the Bharatas, were the sweet words of the men and women, spoken again and again, that he heard.

sanskrit: yājñavalkyasya śiṣyaś ca kuśalo yajñakarmaṇi prāyāt pārthena sahitaḥ śāntyarthaṃ vedapāragaḥ
english: And a disciple of Yājñavalkya, skilled in the rites of sacrifice and versed to the end of the Vedas, set out together with the Pārtha to perform the propitiatory ceremonies.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāś ca mahīpāla bahavo vedapāragāḥ anujagmur mahātmānaṃ kṣatriyāś ca viśo 'pi ca
english: And many Brāhmaṇas, O guardian of the earth, masters of the Vedas, followed that great-souled one, as did Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas too.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavaiḥ pṛthivīm aśvo nirjitām astratejasā cacāra sa mahārāja yathādeśaṃ sa sattama
english: O great king, O most excellent one, that horse roamed over the earth conquered by the Pāṇḍavas through the might of their weapons, wandering at will as ordained.

sanskrit: tatra yuddhāni vṛttāni yāny āsan pāṇḍavasya ha tāni vakṣyāmi te vīra vicitrāṇi mahānti ca
english: The battles that befell the Pāṇḍava there—those I shall recount to you, O hero, wondrous and great as they were.

sanskrit: sa hayaḥ pṛthivīṃ rājan pradakṣiṇam ariṃdama sasārottarataḥ pūrvaṃ tan nibodha mahīpate
english: That horse, O king, O subduer of foes, ranged over the earth keeping it to its right, moving first toward the north—mark this, O guardian of the earth.

sanskrit: avamṛdnan sa rāṣṭrāṇi pārthivānāṃ hayottamaḥ śanais tadā pariyayau śvetāśvaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Trampling down the kingdoms of the rulers of the earth, that finest of horses slowly made his circuit, and with him the great chariot-warrior of the white steeds.

sanskrit: tatra saṃkalanā nāsti rājñām ayutaśas tadā ye 'yudhyanta mahārāja kṣatriyā hatabāndhavāḥ
english: There was no numbering then, O great king, of the kings by the ten thousands—the Kṣatriyas whose kinsmen had been slain—who joined battle there.

sanskrit: kirātā vikṛtā rājan bahavo 'sidhanurdharāḥ mlecchāś cānye bahuvidhāḥ pūrvaṃ vinikṛtā raṇe
english: There were Kirātas of monstrous shape, O king, many bearers of sword and bow, and Mlecchas of various kinds besides, men formerly cut down in battle.

sanskrit: āryāś ca pṛthivīpālāḥ prahṛṣṭanaravāhanāḥ samīyuḥ pāṇḍuputreṇa bahavo yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: And noble rulers of the earth, their men and mounts full of joy, many of them maddened for war, came together to fight the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: evaṃ yuddhāni vṛttāni tatra tatra mahīpate arjunasya mahīpālair nānādeśanivāsibhiḥ
english: Thus, O guardian of the earth, battles took place here and there between Arjuna and the rulers of the earth dwelling in various lands.

sanskrit: yāni tūbhayato rājan prataptāni mahānti ca tāni yuddhāni vakṣyāmi kaunteyasya tavānagha
english: Those great battles, O king, sorely fought out on both sides—those of the son of Kuntī I shall recount to you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca trigartair abhavad yuddhaṃ kṛtavairaiḥ kirīṭinaḥ mahārathasamājñātair hatānāṃ putranaptṛbhiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: A battle befell the Diademed one with the Trigartas, who had nursed their enmity—men renowned as great chariot-warriors, the sons and grandsons of the slain.

sanskrit: te samājñāya saṃprāptaṃ yajñiyaṃ turagottamam viṣayānte tato vīrā daṃśitāḥ paryavārayan
english: Learning that the excellent sacrificial horse had arrived at the border of their realm, those heroes, clad in mail, then surrounded it.

sanskrit: rathino baddhatūṇīrāḥ sadaśvaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaiḥ parivārya hayaṃ rājan grahītuṃ saṃpracakramuḥ
english: Mounted on chariots drawn by fine, well-caparisoned steeds, their quivers bound on, they encircled the horse, O king, and set about to seize it.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭī saṃcintya teṣāṃ rājñāṃ cikīrṣitam vārayām āsa tān vīrān sāntvapūrvam ariṃdamaḥ
english: Then the Diademed one, that subduer of foes, perceiving what those kings intended to do, restrained those heroes with conciliatory words.

sanskrit: tam anādṛtya te sarve śarair abhyahanaṃs tadā tamorajobhyāṃ saṃchannāṃs tān kirīṭī nyavārayat
english: Disregarding him, they all then struck at him with arrows; but the Diademed one held back those who were enveloped in darkness and dust.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tato jiṣṇuḥ prahasann iva bhārata nivartadhvam adharmajñāḥ śreyo jīvitam eva vaḥ
english: And then Jiṣṇu spoke, as if laughing, O Bhārata: "Turn back, you who know not righteousness; your life itself is the better course for you."

sanskrit: sa hi vīraḥ prayāsyan vai dharmarājena vāritaḥ hatabāndhavā na te pārtha hantavyāḥ pārthivā iti
english: For that hero, as he was about to set out, had been enjoined by the King of Righteousness: "O Pārtha, those rulers whose kinsmen have been slain are not to be killed."

sanskrit: sa tadā tad vacaḥ śrutvā dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ tān nivartadhvam ity āha na nyavartanta cāpi te
english: He, then, recalling that word of the wise King of Righteousness, said to them, "Turn back"; yet they did not turn back.

sanskrit: tatas trigartarājānaṃ sūryavarmāṇam āhave vitatya śarajālena prajahāsa dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya, enmeshing in battle the king of the Trigartas, Sūryavarman, in a net of arrows, laughed aloud.

sanskrit: tatas te rathaghoṣeṇa khuranemisvanena ca pūrayanto diśaḥ sarvā dhanaṃjayam upādravan
english: Then they, filling all the quarters with the rumble of their chariots and the clatter of hooves and wheel-rims, rushed upon Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: sūryavarmā tataḥ pārthe śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām śatāny amuñcad rājendra laghvastram abhidarśayan
english: Then Sūryavarman loosed hundreds of straight-jointed arrows at the Pārtha, O lord of kings, displaying the lightness of his hand.

sanskrit: tathaivānye maheṣvāsā ye tasyaivānuyāyinaḥ mumucuḥ śaravarṣāṇi dhanaṃjayavadhaiṣiṇaḥ
english: And likewise the other mighty archers who were his followers, seeking the death of Dhanaṃjaya, poured forth showers of arrows.

sanskrit: sa tāñ jyāpuṅkhanirmuktair bahubhiḥ subahūñ śarān ciccheda pāṇḍavo rājaṃs te bhūmau nyapataṃs tadā
english: With many arrows shot from his bowstring the Pāṇḍava cut down those very many shafts, O king, and they fell upon the ground.

sanskrit: ketuvarmā tu tejasvī tasyaivāvarajo yuvā yuyudhe bhrātur arthāya pāṇḍavena mahātmanā
english: But the fiery Ketuvarman, that king's younger brother, a youth, fought for his brother's sake against the great-souled Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya ketuvarmāṇam āhave abhyaghnan niśitair bāṇair bībhatsuḥ paravīrahā
english: Seeing Ketuvarman bearing down upon him in battle, Bībhatsu, the slayer of hostile heroes, struck him with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: ketuvarmaṇy abhihate dhṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ rathenāśu samāvṛtya śarair jiṣṇum avākirat
english: When Ketuvarman was struck down, the great chariot-warrior Dhṛtavarman, swiftly wheeling round with his chariot, covered Jiṣṇu with arrows.

sanskrit: tasya tāṃ śīghratām īkṣya tutoṣātīva vīryavān guḍākeśo mahātejā bālasya dhṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: Beholding the swiftness of the young Dhṛtavarman, the mighty and greatly fiery Guḍākeśa was exceedingly pleased.

sanskrit: na saṃdadhānaṃ dadṛśe nādadānaṃ ca taṃ tadā kirantam eva sa śarān dadṛśe pākaśāsaniḥ
english: The son of the chastiser of Pāka could not see him nocking nor drawing, but only ever saw him scattering arrows.

sanskrit: sa tu taṃ pūjayām āsa dhṛtavarmāṇam āhave manasā sa muhūrtaṃ vai raṇe samabhiharṣayan
english: He honored Dhṛtavarman in that battle in his mind, and for a moment took delight in him in the fray.

sanskrit: taṃ pannagam iva kruddhaṃ kuruvīraḥ smayann iva prītipūrvaṃ mahārāja prāṇair na vyaparopayat
english: That youth, wrathful as a serpent, the Kuru hero, as if smiling and out of fondness, O great king, did not deprive of his life.

sanskrit: sa tathā rakṣyamāṇo vai pārthenāmitatejasā dhṛtavarmā śaraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ mumoca vijaye tadā
english: Thus spared by the Pārtha of boundless might, Dhṛtavarman then loosed a sharp arrow at Vijaya.

sanskrit: sa tena vijayas tūrṇam asyan viddhaḥ kare bhṛśam mumoca gāṇḍīvaṃ duḥkhāt tat papātātha bhūtale
english: Pierced sorely by it in the hand even as he was swiftly shooting, Vijaya let the Gāṇḍīva slip from his pain, and it fell upon the ground.

sanskrit: dhanuṣaḥ patatas tasya savyasācikarād vibho indrasyevāyudhasyāsīd rūpaṃ bharatasattama
english: As the bow fell from the hand of Savyasācin, O lord, its form was like that of Indra's weapon, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite divye mahādhanuṣi pārthiva jahāsa sasvanaṃ hāsaṃ dhṛtavarmā mahāhave
english: When that divine great bow had fallen, O king, Dhṛtavarman laughed aloud a ringing laugh in that great battle.

sanskrit: tato roṣānvito jiṣṇuḥ pramṛjya rudhiraṃ karāt dhanur ādatta tad divyaṃ śaravarṣaṃ vavarṣa ca
english: Then Jiṣṇu, filled with fury, wiped the blood from his hand, took up that divine bow, and rained down a shower of arrows.

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabdo divaspṛg abhavat tadā nānāvidhānāṃ bhūtānāṃ tat karmātīva śaṃsatām
english: Then a tumultuous uproar arose, touching the heavens, of beings of every kind who exceedingly praised that deed.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃprekṣya taṃ kruddhaṃ kālāntakayamopamam jiṣṇuṃ traigartakā yodhās tvaritāḥ paryavārayan
english: Then, beholding Jiṣṇu wrathful, like Yama the all-ending Death, the Trigarta warriors swiftly surrounded him.

sanskrit: abhisṛtya parīpsārthaṃ tatas te dhṛtavarmaṇaḥ parivavrur guḍākeśaṃ tatrākrudhyad dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Rushing in to rescue Dhṛtavarman, they then hemmed Guḍākeśa about; thereupon Dhanaṃjaya grew wrathful.

sanskrit: tato yodhāñ jaghānāśu teṣāṃ sa daśa cāṣṭa ca mahendravajrapratimair āyasair niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then he swiftly slew eighteen of their warriors with sharp iron arrows like the thunderbolt of great Indra.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu prabhagnān saṃprekṣya tvaramāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ śarair āśīviṣākārair jaghāna svanavad dhasan
english: Seeing them broken, Dhanaṃjaya in haste struck them with arrows shaped like venomous serpents, laughing aloud.

sanskrit: te bhagnamanasaḥ sarve traigartakamahārathāḥ diśo vidudruvuḥ sarvā dhanaṃjayaśarārditāḥ
english: All those great Trigarta chariot-warriors, their spirits broken and tormented by Dhanaṃjaya's arrows, fled in all directions.

sanskrit: ta ūcuḥ puruṣavyāghraṃ saṃśaptakaniṣūdanam tava sma kiṃkarāḥ sarve sarve ca vaśagās tava
english: They said to that tiger among men, the destroyer of the sworn warriors: "We are all your servants, and all of us are subject to your will."

sanskrit: ājñāpayasva naḥ pārtha prahvān preṣyān avasthitān kariṣyāmaḥ priyaṃ sarvaṃ tava kauravanandana
english: "Command us, O Pārtha—we stand here humbled as your servants; we shall do all that pleases you, O delight of the Kurus."

sanskrit: etad ājñāya vacanaṃ sarvāṃs tān abravīt tadā jīvitaṃ rakṣata nṛpāḥ śāsanaṃ gṛhyatām iti
english: Hearing this their word, he then said to them all: "Guard your lives, O kings; let my command be accepted."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prāgjyotiṣam athābhyetya vyacarat sa hayottamaḥ bhagadattātmajas tatra niryayau raṇakarkaśaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, coming to Prāgjyotiṣa, that excellent horse roamed about, and the son of Bhagadatta, fierce in battle, came forth there.

sanskrit: sa hayaṃ pāṇḍuputrasya viṣayāntam upāgatam yuyudhe bharataśreṣṭha vajradatto mahīpatiḥ
english: As the horse of the son of Pāṇḍu reached the border of his realm, King Vajradatta, O best of the Bharatas, gave battle.

sanskrit: so 'bhiniryāya nagarād bhagadattasuto nṛpaḥ aśvam āyāntam unmathya nagarābhimukho yayau
english: Sallying forth from the city, that king, the son of Bhagadatta, drove off the approaching horse and turned back toward the city.

sanskrit: tam ālakṣya mahābāhuḥ kurūṇām ṛṣabhas tadā gāṇḍīvaṃ vikṣipaṃs tūrṇaṃ sahasā samupādravat
english: Marking this, the mighty-armed bull of the Kurus, swiftly twanging the Gāṇḍīva, at once rushed upon him.

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvanirmuktair iṣubhir mohito nṛpaḥ hayam utsṛjya taṃ vīras tataḥ pārtham upādravat
english: Then, stupefied by the shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, that king of a hero released the horse and rushed instead upon the Pārtha.

sanskrit: punaḥ praviśya nagaraṃ daṃśitaḥ sa nṛpottamaḥ āruhya nāgapravaraṃ niryayau yuddhakāṅkṣayā
english: Entering the city again, that best of kings, clad in mail and mounted upon a noble elephant, came forth in his eagerness for battle.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani dodhūyatā cāmareṇa śvetena ca mahārathaḥ
english: With a white parasol held above his head and a white yak-tail fan waving over him, that great chariot-warrior came on.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārthaṃ samāsādya pāṇḍavānāṃ mahāratham āhvayām āsa kauravyaṃ bālyān mohāc ca saṃyuge
english: Then, drawing near to the Pārtha, that great chariot-warrior of the Pāṇḍavas, he challenged the Kaurava to combat, out of youth and folly.

sanskrit: sa vāraṇaṃ nagaprakhyaṃ prabhinnakaraṭāmukham preṣayām āsa saṃkruddhas tataḥ śvetahayaṃ prati
english: Wrathful, he then drove his elephant—huge as a mountain, its temples and cheeks streaming with rut—against him of the white steeds.

sanskrit: vikṣarantaṃ yathā meghaṃ paravāraṇavāraṇam śāstravat kalpitaṃ saṃkhye trisāhaṃ yuddhadurmadam
english: That elephant, pouring forth rut like a raining cloud, a vanquisher of hostile elephants, trained for war according to the science, able to withstand a triple onset and maddened for battle—

sanskrit: pracodyamānaḥ sa gajas tena rājñā mahābalaḥ tadāṅkuśena vibabhāv utpatiṣyann ivāmbaram
english: That mighty elephant, urged on by that king with the goad, appeared as if about to spring up into the sky.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya kruddho rājan dhanaṃjayaḥ bhūmiṣṭho vāraṇagataṃ yodhayām āsa bhārata
english: Seeing it bearing down upon him, the wrathful Dhanaṃjaya, O king, standing on the ground, fought against him who rode upon the elephant, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vajradattas tu saṃkruddho mumocāśu dhanaṃjaye tomarān agnisaṃkāśāñ śalabhān iva vegitān
english: But Vajradatta, full of fury, swiftly loosed at Dhanaṃjaya javelins like fire, hurtling like locusts.

sanskrit: arjunas tān asaṃprāptān gāṇḍīvapreṣitaiḥ śaraiḥ dvidhā tridhā ca ciccheda kha eva khagamais tadā
english: Arjuna, with arrows sped from the Gāṇḍīva—those that fly through the air—cut them apart, two and threefold, in the very sky before they reached him.

sanskrit: sa tān dṛṣṭvā tathā chinnāṃs tomarān bhagadattajaḥ iṣūn asaktāṃs tvaritaḥ prāhiṇot pāṇḍavaṃ prati
english: Seeing his javelins thus cut to pieces, the son of Bhagadatta swiftly hurled at the Pāṇḍava arrows that flew unhindered.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunas tūrṇataraṃ rukmapuṅkhān ajihmagān preṣayām āsa saṃkruddho bhagadattātmajaṃ prati
english: Then Arjuna, more swiftly still and full of wrath, sped against the son of Bhagadatta arrows with golden feathers that flew straight on.

sanskrit: sa tair viddho mahātejā vajradatto mahāhave bhṛśāhataḥ papātorvyāṃ na tv enam ajahāt smṛtiḥ
english: Pierced by them, the greatly fiery Vajradatta, struck hard in that great battle, fell to the earth; yet his consciousness did not forsake him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa punar āruhya vāraṇapravaraṃ raṇe avyagraḥ preṣayām āsa jayārthī vijayaṃ prati
english: Then, mounting his noble elephant once more in the battle, calm and seeking victory, he drove it against Vijaya.

sanskrit: tasmai bāṇāṃs tato jiṣṇur nirmuktāśīviṣopamān preṣayām āsa saṃkruddho jvalitān iva pāvakān
english: Then Jiṣṇu, full of wrath, sped at him arrows like venomous serpents let loose, blazing as flames of fire.

sanskrit: sa tair viddho mahānāgo visravan rudhiraṃ babhau himavān iva śailendro bahuprasravaṇas tadā
english: That great elephant, pierced by them and streaming with blood, then shone like the Himālaya, lord of mountains, with its many cascades.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ trirātram abhavat tad yuddhaṃ bharatarṣabha arjunasya narendreṇa vṛtreṇeva śatakratoḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus for three nights did that battle last, O bull of the Bharatas, between Arjuna and that king, as once between Vṛtra and the Performer of a Hundred Sacrifices.

sanskrit: tataś caturthe divase vajradatto mahābalaḥ jahāsa sasvanaṃ hāsaṃ vākyaṃ cedam athābravīt
english: Then on the fourth day the mighty Vajradatta laughed aloud a ringing laugh and spoke these words:

sanskrit: arjunārjuna tiṣṭhasva na me jīvan vimokṣyase tvāṃ nihatya kariṣyāmi pitus toyaṃ yathāvidhi
english: "Arjuna, Arjuna, stand fast! You shall not escape me alive. Having slain you, I shall make the water-offering to my father according to rule."

sanskrit: tvayā vṛddho mama pitā bhagadattaḥ pituḥ sakhā hato vṛddho 'pacāyitvāc chiśuṃ mām adya yodhaya
english: "By you was my aged father Bhagadatta, the friend of your father, slain—an old man worthy of honor; now do battle with me, who am but a child."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā saṃkruddho vajradatto narādhipaḥ preṣayām āsa kauravya vāraṇaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ prati
english: Having spoken thus, the wrathful King Vajradatta, O Kaurava, drove his elephant against the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: saṃpreṣyamāṇo nāgendro vajradattena dhīmatā utpatiṣyann ivākāśam abhidudrāva pāṇḍavam
english: That lordly elephant, driven on by the sagacious Vajradatta, rushed upon the Pāṇḍava as if about to spring into the sky.

sanskrit: agrahastapramuktena śīkareṇa sa phalgunam samukṣata mahārāja śailaṃ nīla ivāmbudaḥ
english: With the spray flung from the tip of its trunk it drenched Phalguna, O great king, as a dark cloud drenches a mountain.

sanskrit: sa tena preṣito rājñā meghavan ninadan muhuḥ mukhāḍambaraghoṣeṇa samādravata phalgunam
english: Driven on by that king, the elephant, roaring again and again like a cloud, with the trumpeting blare of its mouth charged upon Phalguna.

sanskrit: sa nṛtyann iva nāgendro vajradattapracoditaḥ āsasāda drutaṃ rājan kauravāṇāṃ mahāratham
english: That lordly elephant, as if dancing, urged on by Vajradatta, swiftly closed, O king, with the great chariot-warrior of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya vajradattasya vāraṇam gāṇḍīvam āśritya balī na vyakampata śatruhā
english: Seeing the elephant of Vajradatta bearing down upon him, the strong slayer of foes, relying on the Gāṇḍīva, did not waver.

sanskrit: cukrodha balavac cāpi pāṇḍavas tasya bhūpateḥ kāryavighnam anusmṛtya pūrvavairaṃ ca bhārata
english: And the Pāṇḍava grew exceedingly wrathful at that king, recalling the hindrance to his task and the old enmity, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ vāraṇaṃ kruddhaḥ śarajālena pāṇḍavaḥ nivārayām āsa tadā veleva makarālayam
english: Then the wrathful Pāṇḍava held back that elephant with a net of arrows, as the shore holds back the abode of the crocodiles.

sanskrit: sa nāgapravaro vīryād arjunena nivāritaḥ tasthau śarair vitunnāṅgaḥ śvāvic chalalito yathā
english: That noble elephant, checked by the might of Arjuna, stood still, its body bristling with arrows like a porcupine with its quills.

sanskrit: nivāritaṃ gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagadattātmajo nṛpaḥ utsasarja śitān bāṇān arjune krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: Seeing his elephant checked, the king, the son of Bhagadatta, frenzied with rage, let fly sharp arrows at Arjuna.
